title: The Nuclear Reactors Nobody Built
titleSupport: Only if the live Reel composer exposes a separate title field; otherwise use the post caption without inserting an extra title.
description:
Earth had nuclear reactors roughly two billion years before humans could build them.

At Oklo, in what is now Gabon, geology concentrated uranium and groundwater helped sustain nuclear fission. Scientists uncovered the evidence in 1972.

These were natural reaction zones in rock. They produced heat, not electricity. Starts and stops are inferred from isotope evidence in one studied zone; the heating-and-water feedback is reconstructed.

Original illustrations and AI-generated narration.

#Oklo #Geology
firstComment: Nature didn't build a power station. It brought together fuel, water and geological conditions that allowed a nuclear chain reaction. The starts-and-stops account is a scientific reconstruction from one studied zone.
